references.text: The description of the land flowing with milk and honey is used here ironically by Dathan and Abiram to refer to Egypt, whereas it was originally used by God for the promised land of Canaan.
The Israelites had previously complained that Moses brought them out into the wilderness to die, the same accusation made by Dathan and Abiram here.
The people accused Moses of wanting to kill them in the wilderness, a charge similar to that raised by Dathan and Abiram.
The question of who appointed Moses as ruler and judge over the people was first raised by a Hebrew in Egypt and is now repeated by Dathan and Abiram.
The Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, accusing them of bringing them out to die, the same kind of rebellion seen in this text.
In his speech, Stephen quotes how the Israelites rejected Moses' leadership with the question of who had appointed him as ruler and judge.
Stephen points out that Moses was rejected by the people who asked who had made him their leader, reflecting the rebellion recorded in Numbers.
